title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.35-37). Grothendieck is building an 'algebra of figures': combinatorial objects (cells, polyhedra) modelled by finite (pre)ordered sets.

(1) End of the argument begun on p.35. We have a preordered set I, a subset J of I, and an increasing map h_J : J' -> J. On the set K = J' ⊔ (I∖J) he defines a preorder. It restricts to the given orders on J' and on I∖J. Across the two pieces, α ≤ β (α in J', β in I∖J) iff h_J(α) ≤ β in I. The map h_K : K -> I is h_J on J' and the identity on I∖J. This gives a commutative square J' -> K -> I over J -> I, with J' = h_K^{-1}(J) and K∖J' ≅ I∖J.

The top of p.36 asserts that K is a final (terminal) object among commutative squares J' -i'-> I', h : I' -> I, over J -> I, of (finite) ordered sets satisfying the previous condition. That condition is presumably J' = h^{-1}(J), possibly with h an isomorphism off J'. The comparison map I' -> K is the identity on J' and h on I'∖J'.

This map is monotone exactly because J is a down-set (closed for the Alexandrov topology in his convention). If α ≤ β with β in J', then h(α) ≤ h(β) ∈ J, so h(α) ∈ J and α ∈ J'. So mixed pairs only go from J' to I'∖J', where monotonicity follows from h(α) ≤ h(β). The sentence 'implique (b,c,d) ⇔ a)' closes off a list of equivalent conditions stated on earlier pages (not visible here).

Geometrically, K is the 'modification' of I that replaces the closed subfigure J by J' over it. It is the poset counterpart of gluing a space to a closed piece along a map: the attaching or Artin-gluing pattern, open part I∖J and closed part J'.

(2) Entry of 18 June. Grothendieck decides that the most practical framework is ultra-topologies, i.e. Alexandrov topologies, equivalently preorders. These avoid the worst complications while still letting one work with ordered index sets.

Definition: a figure (in Σ, inside an ambient set L) is a pair (S,T). S is a subset of L and T an ultra-topology on S. He gives three equivalent characterisations of T:
- arbitrary unions of closed sets are closed;
- equivalently, arbitrary intersections of opens are open;
- equivalently, every point has a smallest (necessarily open) neighbourhood.

Two figures (S,T), (S',T') are compatible if T and T' induce the same topology on S∩S', and S∩S' is closed in S and in S'. Then there is a unique topology on S∪S' inducing T and T' with S and S' closed. Next page: this is the final topology, i.e. the pushout S ⊔_{S∩S'} S' along a common closed subspace, and it is again Alexandrov.

The page sets up a partial 'union' operation on figures: gluing finite T0/Alexandrov spaces along closed subspaces. Sub-figures are closed subsets with the induced topology.
errors: The terminality claim for K silently requires J to be closed (a down-set, in his convention) in I, and the 'previous condition' to include J' = h^{-1}(J). Without this the comparison map I' -> K is not monotone. Presumably this hypothesis is in situation (*) on earlier pages.
'(b,c,d) ⇔ a)' refers to conditions not on this page; it cannot be checked here.

Minor: compatibility requires S∩S' closed in both S and S'. That is exactly what makes S and S' closed in the glued space, and gluing along non-closed intersections is not considered. This is consistent, not an error.

ideas.what: Terminal object K = J' ⊔ (I∖J) among squares J'->I' over J->I with J' = h^{-1}(J): the poset 'modification' replacing a closed piece J by J' over it
ideas.modern_name: gluing/attaching of finite posets (Alexandrov spaces) along a closed subset; poset analogue of Artin gluing / attaching map; a right-adjoint-type 'modification'
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in finite-space / poset topology (cf. Artin gluing, SGA4; finite spaces of McCord, Stong)
ideas.where_published: Artin gluing appears in SGA4 (Exposé IV); this poset version is not, as far as I know

ideas.what: Ultra-topology = topology closed under arbitrary intersections of opens = preorder
ideas.where_published: unsure; the term 'ultra-topologie' does not appear in his published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Figures as pairs (S,T), S ⊂ L, T an Alexandrov topology; compatibility and gluing along a common closed subspace (pushout)
ideas.modern_name: pushout of Alexandrov spaces along closed embeddings; finite-space models of CW/polyhedral complexes (face posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard topology; finite-space combinatorial topology (McCord 1966, Stong 1966; Barmak's book)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's unpublished 'algèbre des figures' (1986) chooses Alexandrov spaces, under the name 'ultra-topologies', as the basic framework for combinatorial figures, with a partial union operation given by gluing along closed subspaces. This documents his late interest in finite-space / poset models of polyhedra, which is not reflected in the literature on finite spaces.
missed.quote: Dans toutes ces questions, les ... (i.e. top. préordonnées) prises en vue des ultra-topologies sont peut-être les plus pratiques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it links his 1980s 'tame topology' / figures programme (Esquisse, §5-6) to finite-space topology. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary and standard: Alexandrov topologies, gluing along closed subsets, and a terminal-object property of a poset modification. The only mild interest is historical, namely that Grothendieck adopts finite/Alexandrov spaces under his own term 'ultra-topologie' as the foundation of his 'algebra of figures'.
transcription_corrections: 'on pourra[?] que tout pt a un plus petit voisinage' should read 'ou encore que tout pt a un plus petit voisinage'.
'disons qu'ils sont compatibles si pour[?] que T, T' induisent...' likely reads 'disons qu'ils sont compatibles si (= signifie que) T, T' induisent...'.
First word '-sitivité[?]' is the end of a word split from p.35 (possibly 'transitivité' or a form of 'positivité'); uncertain.
'les Boriennes[?]' is uncertain; the phrase is roughly 'sans présenter les pires types de complications ..., mais prises en termes d'ensembles (d'indices) ordonnés'.
'Une "figure" {+dans Σ[?]+} est couple ... un couple': the inserted symbol may be L, matching 'partie S de L' below.
